text:
Priya Patel: Heads-up: I need to cut out at 17:45 today. Can someone pick up primary from 18:00-22:00? I have an in-progress canary and a pending infra change that I can't finish. Leaving notes below. Please confirm who9s primary and who9s secondary, and that you9ve read the runbook links.

Alex Chen: I can take primary 18:00-20:30. @Sam, can you be secondary and then take over full primary at 20:30? I'll handle the first hour of the canary ramp.

Sam Rodriguez: Yep I9ll be available as secondary and take full at 20:30. Will join at 20:15 for a 15m warm handoff.

incident-bot: reminder: please complete handoff checklist in PagerDuty and paste the handoff note here. Runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/oncall-core

Priya Patel: Handoff note pasted to PD. Active alerts: runtime-cpu-surge (warning), embeddings-queue-backlog (watch), canary-errors (deploy flagged). Deploy plan at 19:50 with canary ramp. If canary error rate >0.75% over 2 mins, pause rollout. See my short commands: `./deployctl pause --canary` and `./deployctl rollback --service=embedding-service --to=2026-03-02`.

Maria Gomez: Quick escalation rules to keep in mind: 
- P0: Severe customer impact / outage. Page primary and secondary immediately, create bridge within 3m, notify Eng Director if bridge not formed in 5m.
- P1: High customer impact. Page primary; if no ACK in 5m escalate to secondary and oncall lead.
- P2: Degraded but non-critical. Page primary and log incident in #incidents.
Also: for any data-loss suspicion escalate to Jordan immediately.

Alex Chen: Logging my watch list: watching error % and tail latencies. My immediate mitigation steps if I get paged: 1) check Grafana overview -> last 5m errors/latencies, 2) check PD payload for context, 3) open bridge if user-facing, 4) run `./scripts/healthcheck.sh all` and collect `journalctl -u runtime -n 1000`.

Sam Rodriguez: I'll add this to my checklist too. For memory-pressure triggered evictions, two mitigations: temporary node pool scale with `infractl scale --pool=spot-ephemeral --count=3` or bump JVM heap on svc via svc-config. If you scale, make sure to watch GC times.

Priya Patel: Note: the embeddings queue backlog is likely due to a downstream ingest lag. Temporarily set the consumer concurrency to 6 (from 12) to reduce pressure on the cache. Command: `kubectl -n services set env deploy/emb-consumer CONCURRENCY=6`. Revert after backlog clears.

Maria Gomez: Paging etiquette reminder: use PD with short context (1-2 lines), include last 5m metric snapshot and suspected impact. First escalation: primary (sms+push). If no response escalate to secondary (+call) then oncall lead (phone). For urgent P0 you can bypass and DM Jordan.

Jordan Mills: I'll be available by phone for escalations tonight. If a P0 happens and I9m not on the bridge in 3 minutes, DM me and I9ll join via Zoom. I9ll take ownership of external comms if needed.

Alex Chen: Small note about the 19:50 deploy: the canary runs on two hosts. If error spike appears on only one host, drain and reprovision rather than rolling back immediately. Draining command: `kubectl drain host-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. If both hosts show errors, follow rollback plan.

Sam Rodriguez: At 20:15 I'll do a short handoff: confirm PD escalation policy set, verify runbook link, confirm which alerts are muted or in watch mode, and list any TODOs.

Priya Patel: Done. I left host IDs for suspect hosts and the small snapshot of logs: `grep ERROR /var/log/services/embeddings.log | tail -n 50`. Also flagged the SLO dashboard: https://go/redwood/grafana/slo-overview.

incident-bot: auto-note: handoff checklist shows PD note added, active incidents flagged: embeddings-queue-backlog (watch), canary-errors (flagged).

Alex Chen: Thanks. I9ll post status updates in this thread if I take any mitigation steps during my window. If I need Jordan, I9ll page directly.

Sam Rodriguez: Good plan. If I9m primary and we get a P1 that9s customer-impacting, I9ll open the bridge and tag #incidents; Jordan if you can lead comms that'd be great.

Maria Gomez: One more operational tip: if you open a bridge, drop a short runbook pointer `RB-401 - transient latency` into the bridge chat to save time. That runbook has the quick triage commands and the rollback script.

Priya Patel: Leaving now. Thanks everyone 44b. Ping me up until 17:50 if you need anything.

Alex Chen: Acknowledged. Taking over at 18:00.

Sam Rodriguez: I9ll join for warm handoff at 20:15 and take over 20:30.

Jordan Mills: Standby and good handoff. Keep me posted if anything degrades.
